harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Tonic chord establishing the dark minor key center
F# (V) - Major dominant chord borrowed from B harmonic minor, provides strong resolution tendency
A (VII) - Subtonic chord creating smooth stepwise motion from the tonic
E (IV) - Subdominant providing harmonic movement and tension
G (VI) - Submediant adding brightness and contrast within the minor key
D (III) - Mediant serving as relative major, creating a sense of lift
Em (iv) - Minor subdominant adding depth before resolving to V
The progression creates a descending chromatic Walking bass line pattern

techniques.name: 12-String Acoustic Arpeggios
techniques.description: The iconic intro and verse pattern played on a 12-string acoustic guitar, using fingerpicked arpeggios to outline each chord in the progression with a shimmering, full-bodied sound

notes: Bm: X-2-4-4-3-2 (Barre chord at 2nd fret)
F#: 2-4-4-3-2-2 (Barre chord at 2nd fret)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (Open A major)
E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (Open E major)
Each chord is arpeggiated with a specific picking pattern rather than strummed
The 12-string doubles each note an octave higher for the signature shimmering sound
Thumb handles bass notes while fingers pick upper strings in sequence
sequence: Play bass note of each chord with thumb
Pick through upper strings in ascending pattern
Maintain steady eighth-note pulse at 75 BPM
Transition smoothly between chord shapes while arpeggios ring
tips: Practice on a 6-string first to get the fingerpicking pattern down before moving to 12-string
Focus on letting each note ring cleanly into the next
Use a thumb pick or fingerpicks for clarity on a 12-string
Keep fretting hand close to frets for clean barre chord voicings

techniques.name: Dual Guitar Harmony Solo
techniques.description: One of the most celebrated guitar solos in rock history, featuring two electric guitars playing harmonized lead lines in thirds and sixths over the verse progression, building from lyrical phrases to blazing runs

notes: Two guitar parts harmonized primarily in diatonic thirds within B minor
Guitar 1 plays the higher melody line while Guitar 2 plays a harmonized lower part
Uses B natural minor, B harmonic minor, and B minor pentatonic scales
Features string bending, vibrato, legato runs, and position shifts across the fretboard
The solo builds in intensity from melodic phrases to faster scale runs
sequence: First section: lyrical melodic phrases with bends and vibrato around 7th-10th frets
Second section: harmonized ascending runs building intensity
Third section: faster scale runs and climactic phrases around 12th-15th frets
Final section: both guitars converge on unison bends for the dramatic conclusion
tips: Learn each guitar part separately before attempting to play along with the recording
Focus on matching the phrasing and vibrato style of the original
Practice the harmony intervals in isolation to understand the third/sixth relationships
Use a metronome at slower tempos to nail the rhythmic precision of the harmonized runs
details.progression: Over Bm - F# - A - E - G - D - Em - F# progression

techniques.name: Chord Arpeggiation and Fingerpicking
techniques.description: Clean fingerpicking technique used throughout the song to arpeggiate full chord voicings, creating a flowing harmonic tapestry beneath the vocal melody

notes: G: 3-2-0-0-3-3 (Open G with fingers on low E and high E strings)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (Open D major)
Use thumb (p) for bass strings 6-4 and index (i), middle (m), ring (a) for strings 3-1
Maintain consistent dynamics across all picked strings
sequence: Anchor thumb on bass string of each chord
Pick strings 3, 2, 1 in ascending order with i, m, a fingers
Return to bass note to begin next beat
Keep a steady pulse while allowing notes to sustain and overlap
tips: Practice the picking pattern on a single chord before adding changes
Keep fingernails trimmed and shaped for consistent tone
Focus on even volume between thumb bass notes and finger-picked treble notes
Let notes ring as long as possible for the full arpeggiated effect

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The iconic 12-string acoustic intro playing arpeggiated chords through the full 8-chord progression, establishing the haunting atmosphere of the song
sections.progression: Bm - F# - A - E - G - D - Em - F#
notes: 12-string acoustic guitar carries the entire intro
Each chord arpeggiated with a consistent fingerpicking pattern
Bass line descends chromatically: B - A# - A - G# - G - F# - E - F#
Two full cycles of the progression before vocals enter

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse sections continue the arpeggiated pattern beneath the vocal melody, with subtle variations and a second guitar adding light accompaniment
sections.progression: Bm - F# - A - E - G - D - Em - F#
notes: Same chord progression as the intro with arpeggiated accompaniment
Dynamics stay controlled to support the vocal melody
Second guitar may add subtle chord stabs or fills
Maintain even tempo at 75 BPM throughout

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus reorders the progression starting on G major, with fuller strumming and increased dynamics as the song builds intensity
sections.progression: G - D - F# - Bm - G - D - Em - F#
notes: Progression starts on G (VI) rather than Bm for a brighter, more open feel
Strumming becomes fuller compared to verse arpeggios
Dynamic lift signals the chorus energy shift
Vocal harmonies layer over the chord progression

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the greatest guitar solos in rock history, featuring Don Felder and Joe Walsh trading harmonized lead lines over the verse progression, building from melodic phrases to intense dual-guitar harmonies
sections.progression: Bm - F# - A - E - G - D - Em - F# (repeating)
notes: Solo begins with melodic phrases primarily in B minor pentatonic
Dual harmonies enter in diatonic thirds within B natural minor
Builds from lyrical phrasing to faster scalar runs
Features bending, vibrato, legato, and position shifts across the neck
Considered one of the greatest guitar solos of all time

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The song concludes with the dual guitar harmonies continuing over the repeating progression, fading out as the solo intensifies
sections.progression: Bm - F# - A - E - G - D - Em - F# (repeating to fade)
notes: Continuation of the dual harmony solo section
Intensifying guitar lines as the song fades
No definitive ending - the music fades out while the solo continues
Both guitars trade and harmonize increasingly complex lines

alternatives: Fender Stratocaster or Gibson SG for electric parts
6-string acoustic can approximate the intro with capo techniques
guitar.pickup: Humbuckers for electric parts, piezo or condenser mic for acoustic

effects.distortion: None to light overdrive for solo sections
effects.reverb: Medium spring or hall reverb for ambience
effects.other: Light chorus for shimmer on clean parts, slight delay for solo sustain

beginner.title: Getting Started with Hotel California
steps: Learn the basic open chord shapes: A, E, G, D, Em
Practice the Bm and F# barre chord shapes
Work on simple fingerpicking patterns on a single chord
Practice transitioning between the 8 chords in sequence slowly

intermediate.title: Building the Arpeggiated Foundation
steps: Master the full arpeggiated intro pattern at slow tempo
Learn the verse and chorus chord progressions with proper voicings
Practice fingerpicking patterns with a metronome at 50-60 BPM
Build speed gradually toward the 75 BPM target tempo
Work on smooth barre chord transitions throughout the progression

advanced.title: Mastering the Solo and Full Performance
steps: Learn the lead guitar solo melody line note for note
Practice the harmony guitar part separately
Work on dual harmony intervals and phrasing
Develop bending, vibrato, and legato techniques for solo authenticity
Combine all sections for a complete performance

commonMistakes: Rushing the arpeggiated intro - maintain the slow 75 BPM tempo
Sloppy barre chord shapes causing buzzing or muted strings
Not letting arpeggiated notes ring into each other for the flowing sound
Ignoring the harmonic minor inflection on the F# chord (should feel distinctly major)
Playing the solo too fast without capturing the melodic phrasing
practiceRoutine: Warm up with Bm and F# barre chord transitions for 5 minutes
Practice the full 8-chord arpeggio pattern at 50 BPM for 10 minutes
Work on the chord progression with a metronome, increasing 5 BPM each session
Practice solo phrases in short 4-bar segments at slow tempo
Play along with the original recording once comfortable at full speed
focusAreas: Clean barre chord voicings across all 8 chords
Consistent fingerpicking pattern with even dynamics
Smooth chord transitions without gaps in the arpeggiated flow
Accurate pitch on string bends during the solo
Understanding the harmonic minor V chord relationship
metronomeWork: Start arpeggios at 50 BPM and increase by 5 BPM per session
Target tempo is 75 BPM - do not exceed this
Practice chord changes on beats 1 and 3 at half tempo first
Use subdivision clicks (eighth notes) to ensure even arpeggio timing
Work solo phrases at 40-50 BPM before building to song tempo
